docs.title: Yu — CLI and Developer Manual
docs.text:
yu is an agent harness with a decision layer. The decision layer holds the human's intent and the run's state; execution is delegated to disposable agents that are told what they need and are not expected to remember anything.

This manual documents the command surface, the files it reads and writes, and the interfaces an integrator builds against. It does not document the design rationale; that lives in the repository.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Audience Start at Operating yu from a shell Installation → Commands Writing policy or reading records Policy file · Record format Building against the crates or the socket Embedding the crates Pointing yu at a non-Anthropic endpoint Endpoint compatibility

docs.title: Command map
docs.text:
Command Purpose Calls a model Writes a record yu probe Measure what the endpoint supports yes no yu exec One request, straight to the wire yes no yu run One task through the execution loop yes yes yu decide The decision layer on a charter yes yes yu metrics Summarise a recorded session no no yu fork Branch a record at a historical point no marker only yu daemon Serve sessions over a Unix socket no yes

yu exec and yu run are the two ends of the same axis. exec is the short path: one request, no session, no journal, no tools. run is the long path: it stands up a session and writes a record, which is exactly the cost exec exists to avoid.

docs.title: Minimum viable run
docs.text:
1. Build the binary. See Installation.

  2. Export a credential.

    export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...

  3. Confirm the endpoint answers.

    yu exec -p "reply ok"

  4. Run one task with no side effects. The read-only tool surface is the default and cannot change anything.

    yu run --task "count the Rust source files under crates/" --cwd .

  5. Read back what was recorded.

    yu metrics --dir .yu

--tools full adds exec

The full tool surface adds write_file and exec. exec runs sh -c with no sandbox, no timeout, and no path restriction, under the environment of the calling process. It can do anything the process can. See Tools.

docs.title: Conventions used in this manual
docs.text:
• $VAR denotes an environment variable. See Configuration.
  • Values shown in --flag <VALUE> form are literal, including the case.
  • A path like .yu/ is relative to the process working directory unless stated otherwise.
  • Exit status is 0 on success and 1 on any runtime error. Argument-parsing failures exit 2. See Exit status.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: yu reads no configuration file. All configuration is environment variables and command-line flags.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Read by Default when unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY credential — ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN credential, used only if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset — ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL endpoint https://api.anthropic.com ANTHROPIC_MODEL default model claude-opus-5 YU_QUIRKS_JSON path to a saved endpoint profile — YU_QUIRKS named endpoint profile, used only if YU_QUIRKS_JSON is unset unknown

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
Set exactly one. Both are sent as the x-api-key header; the two names exist because different deployments issue different shapes of secret, not because they are sent differently.

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...

No credential is a hard failure

With neither variable set, the client fails immediately:

no credential: set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN

Credentials are redacted from the client's Debug output and are never written to a record. The endpoint itself is less careful — a 401 response body echoes the last four characters of the key it received. Treat captured error bodies as sensitive. See Quirk 6.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic

The endpoint must speak the Anthropic Messages API. It need not be Anthropic's, and it need not honour everything Anthropic honours — that is what the quirks profile is for.

Before pointing yu at an endpoint, measure it:

yu probe

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
Resolution order, highest first:

  1. --model on the command line
  2. ANTHROPIC_MODEL
  3. claude-opus-5
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5

The model string is sent verbatim. yu does not validate it against a list and does not map between names.

docs.title: Endpoint profile (quirks)
docs.text:
The endpoint profile records which of the Messages API's behaviours the endpoint actually has. It is not cosmetic: it decides whether history must carry thinking blocks, whether identifiers may be synthesised, and whether cache_control does anything.

There are two ways to set it, and YU_QUIRKS_JSON wins.

Measured — preferred. Write the report from a probe and read it back.

yu probe --json > caps.json
export YU_QUIRKS_JSON=$PWD/caps.json

Named — a shortcut, unverified against your endpoint.

export YU_QUIRKS=anthropic
Name Meaning anthropic Anthropic's own behaviour deepseek-anthropic, deepseek The measured behaviour of https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic unknown Assumes the strict rules. The default when nothing is set

A profile that fails to load does not stop the run

If YU_QUIRKS_JSON names a file that cannot be read or parsed, the client logs an error and falls back to the unknown profile — it does not abort. The run then proceeds under constraints nobody chose. Check the log if a run behaves as though the endpoint were stricter than it is.

docs.title: State directory
docs.text:
Commands that read or write records take --dir, default .yu. It holds the journals and the blob store.

.yu/
  <session>.jsonl
  blobs/<2 hex>/<62 hex>

--dir is not the working directory of the tools

--dir is where records live. --cwd is the directory the tools operate in, and it defaults to the process working directory. --cwd defaults to the directory you launched yu from, not to --dir. A run with --dir /var/yu and no --cwd reads and writes files under the current directory and keeps its journal in /var/yu.

--cwd is available on yu run and yu decide. yu probe, yu exec, yu metrics, yu fork, and yu daemon do not take it.

Add .yu/ to .gitignore. Journals contain model conversations, tool output, and file contents read during the run.

docs.title: Span output
docs.text: Span timings are printed to stderr by the commands that produce them, and a run that recorded none prints spans: NONE RECORDED (observation is not wired up) rather than an empty line. The observation surface has no environment variable: spans are always emitted, and per-step harness overhead is always reported. See yu run.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Item Requirement Rust 1.85 or later — the workspace uses edition 2024 Network Reachable Messages API endpoint Credential ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN

There is no published binary and no package on crates.io. Build from source.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/ChenyuHeee/Yu.git
cd Yu
cargo build --release

The binary is target/release/yu.

./target/release/yu --version

To install it on PATH:

cargo install --path crates/yu-cli

Release profile

The release profile sets lto = "thin", codegen-units = 1, and debug = 1. Building in release mode matters if per-step overhead is what you are measuring; a debug build reports the debug build's overhead.

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
Confirm the binary runs and the endpoint answers. This step costs one model request.

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
yu exec -p "reply ok"

Expected: the model's reply on stdout, exit status 0.

If no credential is set, the client fails with:

no credential: set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN

docs.title: Measure the endpoint before trusting it
docs.text:
yu probe asks the endpoint which fields it actually honours. Run it once against any endpoint that is not Anthropic's; the result decides which features the rest of the manual applies to.

yu probe

See yu probe and Endpoint compatibility.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: yu writes records to disk. Records are read back by yu metrics, yu fork, and session continuation. A record written by an older build decodes under a newer one as long as the event envelope is unchanged; yu metrics skips any line it cannot parse rather than failing. See Record format.

docs.title: Commands — conventions
docs.text: Conventions that apply to every subcommand. Individual pages document only what is specific to them.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
yu <COMMAND> [OPTIONS]

Run yu <COMMAND> --help for the authoritative option list of the build in front of you.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text:
Status Meaning 0 Success 1 Any runtime error. The error text is printed to stderr as yu: <message> 2 Argument parsing failed. Emitted by the argument parser before the command runs

There are no other statuses, and no command defines a command-specific one. A run that stops early for an operational reason — the round ceiling was reached, a budget was spent — is a successful run: it reports stopped: <reason> and exits 0. Only a failure to run at all exits 1.

docs.title: Output streams
docs.text:
Every command that produces both an answer and a report separates them.

Stream Carries stdout The result: the model's reply, the assembled blocks, or the metrics summary stderr Everything else: the --- report lines, warnings, progress 
# The answer alone.
yu run --task "..." 2>/dev/null

# The report alone.
yu run --task "..." >/dev/null

docs.title: Shared options
docs.text:
Option Default Applies to Meaning --dir <DIR> .yu run, decide, metrics, fork, daemon Where journals and blobs live --cwd <CWD> process working directory run, decide The directory the tools operate in --model <MODEL> $ANTHROPIC_MODEL, else claude-opus-5 exec, run, decide Model string, sent verbatim --tools <SET> read-only run, decide read-only or full --policy <PATH> none run, decide A policy TOML file

--dir and --cwd are different directories

--dir holds records. --cwd is where tools read and write. Neither implies the other. See Configuration.

docs.title: Tool sets
docs.text:
Value Tools granted read-only read_file, list_dir full read_file, write_file, list_dir, exec

read-only is the default on both commands that take the flag. The executor's surface is printed on start:

--- tool surface: list_dir, read_file

See Tools for the schemas.

docs.title: Session naming
docs.text:
A session is an address on disk. Sessions are named, and naming one is how a run is found again after it ends, including when it ends by kill -9.

Command Name when --session is not given yu run run-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS yu decide decide-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS

The timestamp is UTC and has one-second resolution.

Give long-running work an explicit session name

The generated name is minted when the run starts. A run that is killed cannot be continued unless its name was known in advance. Pass --session for anything that should survive a crash:

yu decide --session delivery-1 --charter "..."

A second run under the same name at the same second would otherwise collide. yu decide refuses a same-second collision rather than silently forking a session onto itself.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Commands that run a model print a report to stderr. Common line shapes:

Line Meaning --- tokens in=… out=… cache_read=… Token usage for the run --- spans: <kind>=<ms> … Per-span timings, or NONE RECORDED --- decision layer context: raw material N% of M chars (…) Composition of the decision layer's context --- executor context: raw material N% of M chars (…) The same, for one executor

raw material is the fraction of a context that arrived as unjudged tool output. It is the number the decision layer's design is judged by; see yu decide.

docs.title: yu daemon
docs.text: Serve sessions over a Unix socket, owning the records they live in.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: yu daemon [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning --dir <DIR> .yu Where sessions keep their journals and descriptions --socket <SOCKET> .yu/daemon.sock The socket the protocol is served on

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Binds a Unix socket and serves the session protocol on it, in the foreground. The session belongs to the daemon, not to the client that started it, so a client that dies does not take the session with it.

On start:

--- daemon up: sessions in .yu, protocol on .yu/daemon.sock

If the socket path is already occupied by a live daemon, it refuses to start. If the path holds a socket that nobody is serving — what kill -9 leaves behind — it says so and rebinds:

--- .yu/daemon.sock is a socket nobody is serving: the daemon that bound it is gone (a kill -9 leaves exactly this). Rebinding.

Nothing is attached at start-up. Sessions are read from disk per request, so a daemon that opened every journal eagerly would repair every torn tail before anyone asked.

The daemon does not run model turns

send records the human's words into the session's journal. It does not call a model, and the daemon never constructs a client. The daemon can resume a session and record into it, but nothing here executes a turn.

yu run and yu decide are separate processes that open their own journals. They do not go through the daemon.

docs.title: Session storage
docs.text:
The daemon uses a different on-disk layout from the CLI. Each session gets its own directory:

.yu/
  daemon.sock
  <session-id>/
    info.json           session description: status, timestamps, last seq
    <session-id>.jsonl  the journal
    blobs/<2 hex>/<62 hex>

Compare Record format. A consequence worth knowing: yu metrics reads only top-level *.jsonl files and will not summarise daemon-owned sessions.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
Framing. One JSON object per line, newline-terminated, in both directions. A blank line is skipped. A malformed line is answered with an error frame rather than closing the connection.

No client subcommand exists. yu has no attach, send, or status command. Speak the protocol directly, or write a client against yu_server::session::{Request, Response, encode_line, decode_line}.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text:
Every frame carries a type discriminator.

Frame Fields Effect {"type":"start","charter":"…"} charter Starts a session. Answers started {"type":"resume","session":"s-1"} session Reattaches to a session the daemon owns, including one it is recovering. Answers status — not started {"type":"send","session":"s-1","text":"…"} session, text Records the text as a user message. Answers chunk then done {"type":"stop","session":"s-1"} session Marks the session stopped. Answers done {"type":"status","session":"s-1"} session, or null for all Answers status

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Frame Fields {"type":"started","session":"s-1"} session {"type":"chunk","session":"s-1","text":"…"} A piece of streamed output {"type":"done","session":"s-1","stop_reason":"…"} stop_reason, carried verbatim {"type":"error","message":"…"} The failure {"type":"status","sessions":[ … ]} A list of SessionInfo

stop_reason is never flattened to a generic "finished". The daemon's own values are:

Value Emitted by recorded send — the message was recorded stopped stop

A send answers with an explicit statement that no turn ran:

recorded at seq 12; running the turn needs a model client, which `yu-server` deliberately does not construct

docs.title: SessionInfo
docs.text:
{
  "id": "s1759000000000-1",
  "status": "ready",
  "created_ms": 1759000000000,
  "last_active_ms": 1759000001234,
  "journal_dir": ".yu/s1759000000000-1",
  "last_seq": 12
}

status is one of starting, ready, busy, stopped, or an object for a crash: {"crashed":{"at_ms":1759000009999}}. A crash is reported with a wall-clock timestamp rather than a duration, so it stays comparable with journal timestamps across daemon restarts.

last_seq is the last sequence number that decodes. It is absent when the host keeps no record, which is not the same as a record that is empty.

docs.title: Talking to it
docs.text:
yu daemon --dir .yu &
socat - UNIX-CONNECT:.yu/daemon.sock

Then, one frame per line:

{"type":"start","charter":"Deliver report.sh in this directory."}
{"type":"status","session":null}
{"type":"send","session":"s1759000000000-1","text":"Begin."}
{"type":"stop","session":"s1759000000000-1"}

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status Condition 0 The daemon shut down cleanly 1 The socket is served by a live daemon, or binding failed

docs.title: yu decide
docs.text: Run the decision layer on a charter.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: yu decide [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning -c, --charter <CHARTER> required for a new session What is to be achieved, in the human's own words --dir <DIR> .yu Where the journal and blobs live --cwd <CWD> process working directory The directory the tools operate in -m, --model <MODEL> $ANTHROPIC_MODEL, else claude-opus-5 Model string --max-rounds <N> 4 for a new session; otherwise what the session has left Round ceiling --tools <SET> read-only Tool surface offered to executors --policy <PATH> none Policy TOML supplying prediction sets and reduction rows --constraint <TEXT> none A standing constraint. Repeat for several --topology <KIND> none The declared shape of the work --session <NAME> decide-<UTC timestamp> The session this run belongs to. Conflicts with --handover --handover <PATH> none Start from a handover an earlier session wrote --handover-out <PATH> none Write a handover for the next session here, when this run ends --handover-at-growth <N> none Also hand over once the view has grown this many characters. Requires --handover-out

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Runs a layer whose job is to decide rather than to do. It is given the charter, your constraints, and the state it has accumulated; it cannot read files, run commands, or see raw tool output. Everything that touches the world is handed to a fresh executor as a delegation.

The layer's own tools are delegate, decide, retire, and spot_check. It has no read_file, no write_file, and no exec. See Tools.

ask_human is specified and not built. Calling it returns an unknown-tool error naming the four that exist.

docs.title: The charter
docs.text:
The charter is the human's intent, word for word. It is not a task description and not a summary.

yu decide --charter "Explain why check.py fails. Report the cause; change nothing."

For a new session, --charter is required. When continuing a session with --session, it is optional: the recorded intent is restored from the record. When it is given on a continuation, it is appended to the recorded intent as a further sentence — it does not replace what was there.

docs.title: Standing constraints
docs.text:
--constraint takes one constraint. Repeat the flag for several.

yu decide \
  --charter "Add a --dry-run flag to the CLI." \
  --constraint "Never modify files outside crates/yu-cli." \
  --constraint "Do not change the exit statuses." \
  --tools full

Constraints are injected into every executor's system block, not restated by the decision layer each round. This is the difference between a constraint that holds and one that is dropped on the round nobody remembered to repeat it. Removing a constraint from the charter changes what the executors are told, and the executor is not given any constraint it was not told.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
--topology declares the shape of the work.

Value Shape single One executor chain Sequential hand-off, each step narrower fan_out One parent, N parallel children. Alias: fanout tree Recursive decomposition reflection Author → critic → author peer Coordination through a message board verification_partition Every work item verified exactly once, by a non-author

--topology takes a kind, not a policy entry name

The value is parsed as a topology kind. If the policy file declares [topology.review_loop], passing --topology review_loop fails — the policy entry is not looked up by name. Pass --topology chain.

An unrecognised value fails with the list of shapes.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
--policy supplies prediction sets and reduction rows. The prediction sets are what a delegation's report is classified against.

yu decide --charter "…" --policy policy.toml

At start the run prints what it loaded:

--- policy policy.toml — 2 outcome set(s): build_result, delivery

With no sets declared, delegations are not classified and no landing can be checked:

--- no prediction sets declared: delegations will not be classified, and no landing can be checked

A continuation whose policy differs from the one the session started under says so, and runs with the newly loaded sets. See Policy file.

docs.title: Sessions and continuation
docs.text:
--session names the run. A name with a record already under it is continued, and the run states what it rebuilt:

--- continuing a session whose record already existed: seq continues at 36; L0 = 1 constraint(s); L1 = 1 decision(s), 0 rejected, 0 open question(s), rebuilt from 3 recorded call(s)
--- rounds already spent: 1; this continuation runs rounds 2..=4

A name with no record starts one, and says so differently, so a name that was not the one you meant shows up as a new session rather than as a continuation of nothing:

--- session delivery-1: no events recorded yet — this run starts it, and a later run with the same name can continue it

Whatever the record cannot supply is named rather than guessed:

--- NOT restored from the record: <problem>

The round budget belongs to the session. A continuation runs what is left of it, not a second helping. If the record holds no round marker, the run says the budget is unknown and runs the whole of what it was given.

Name a session before you need to resume it

A run can only be continued under a name it was given when it started. A session killed before it wrote anything cannot be resumed, and a handover does not help — a handover is written when a session ends, and a killed session wrote none.

--session conflicts with --handover. Starting from a handover branches from the record the handover indexes; continuing a session reopens its own record. They are different operations and cannot both be requested.

docs.title: Handover
docs.text:
A handover carries a session's intent, constraints, decisions, and loose ends to a new generation, with an index of where each item came from.

# Generation 1: run, and write a handover when it ends.
yu decide --charter "…" --session gen1 --handover-out handover.json

# Generation 2: start from it.
yu decide --handover handover.json --session gen2

On start from a handover:

--- resuming from a handover: 1 item(s) carried, 5 angle(s) reported, index at blob:6f97f7…

On writing one:

--- handover (<trigger>): 3 item(s) from 5 angle(s), index at blob:… → handover.json
Trigger When it fires completion The session reached a final answer round ceiling The session spent its round budget without one growth --handover-at-growth <N> and the view grew N characters past where it started

A session that reached its round ceiling hands over without --handover-at-growth. The growth rule covers a session that stopped for any other reason.

Growth, not window size

--handover-at-growth measures growth past the starting point, not the size of the view. A freshly seeded view is large by construction, so a rule written against total size would fire immediately and keep firing.

When a handover was requested but did not fire:

--- no handover: <reason>, and its view did not grow past the declared growth threshold either — this boundary did not warrant the change

A handover does not carry everything. What it left out is printed:

--- the handover does not carry: <text> [<address>]

The address resolves back to the record through the same path spot_check uses.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text: stdout carries the layer's final answer. Everything below goes to stderr.

docs.title: The context report
docs.text:
--- decision layer context: raw material 0.0% of 24531 chars (raw 0 + reduced 6490 + calls 0 + definitions 4278; tool machinery 44.4%)

raw material is the fraction of the context that arrived as unjudged tool output. It is the number the decision layer's premise is judged by: near zero means the layer is holding decisions, not evidence.

docs.title: Per-request growth
docs.text:
--- decision-layer context per request: 10127 23433 31342 29034 29859 29557
--- peak context: 31342 chars, raw material 0.0%

Sizes in characters, one per request, in order. It rises within a round as the conversation grows and falls when the next round re-renders the view. peak is the worst point of the run, not the last one.

docs.title: Landings
docs.text:
--- landings
      #0 delivery/delivered_and_verified — the executor ran report.sh and it printed every file
      #1 build_result/compile_error — the compiler rejected the trait bound (the executor called it `build_broke`)
      #2 not classified (no set was pre-registered)
      !! the executor landed on `delivered_and_verified`, but a command ran and failed: `echo …` exited 1

Each line is one delegation: the slot it landed in, and why. !! marks a contradiction — a landing the harness checked against the record and found inconsistent. This check is deterministic and runs on every delegation; the decision layer is shown the contradiction rather than the raw evidence.

An honest landing produces no !! line. A check that fired on correct runs would be worth nothing.

docs.title: Agent tree
docs.text:
--- agents: 2 derived
      decision
        └ executor#1 — RUNTIME: reproduce the failure of check.py and identify the …
          └ executor#1.1 — Read the file `.yu/decide-….jsonl` in the curr…

Read from the record, not from memory. Derivation stops at 3 levels below the decision layer; an executor at the ceiling is not offered delegate, and a call to it anyway is answered with the ceiling it hit. See Delegation depth.

docs.title: Ledger (L1)
docs.text:
--- L1: 2 decision(s), 2 rejected, 0 open question(s)
      decided: record what you conclude before you answer — because …
      ruled out: a third read-only pass re-deriving the cause — because …

When the layer recorded nothing:

      (the run wrote nothing to state: it reached no conclusion it was willing to record)

docs.title: Stopping early
docs.text:
--- stopped: <reason>

A run that spends its round ceiling is a successful run that stopped early, not a failure. The exit status is 0.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Read-only investigation, four rounds:

yu decide \
  --charter "Explain why check.py fails. Report the cause; change nothing." \
  --cwd . --tools read-only

A named, resumable session with constraints and a topology:

yu decide \
  --session delivery-1 \
  --charter "Deliver report.sh in this directory." \
  --constraint "Work only inside the current directory; never modify anything outside it." \
  --topology chain \
  --policy policy.toml \
  --tools full

Continue it after a crash:

yu decide --session delivery-1

docs.title: yu exec
docs.text: One request, straight to the wire. The short-path bypass.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: yu exec --prompt <PROMPT> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning -p, --prompt <PROMPT> required The prompt -m, --model <MODEL> $ANTHROPIC_MODEL, else claude-opus-5 Model string --max-tokens <N> 4096 Output token ceiling for the response --show-thinking off Stream the model's reasoning summary as it arrives --timing off Print timings to stderr --json off Print the assembled content blocks as JSON

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Sends one request and streams the reply to stdout. It deliberately does not touch sessions, journals, tools, or policy:

  • No session is created and no record is written.
  • No tools are offered. A tool_use block in the response is returned, never executed.
  • No policy file is read.
  • No reduction is applied. The reply is emitted as it arrives.

This is what a short task should cost. yu run exists for everything that needs a record, and it pays for that record on every step.

docs.title: Thinking
docs.text:
Thinking is always requested, with its display set to summarized. --show-thinking controls whether the summary is shown, not whether it is requested. Without the flag the summary is streamed and discarded.

Thinking blocks are part of the response, not decoration

On endpoints that require it, an assistant turn containing tool_use must be sent back with its thinking block intact. yu exec does not replay anything, so this does not arise here — but it is why the field is requested at all. See Quirk 1.

docs.title: --timing
docs.text:
Prints to stderr:

--- stop=<STOP_REASON> in=<N> out=<N> cache_read=<N> attempts=<N>
--- wire_wait=<ms> first_token=<ms> stream=<ms> events=<N> text=<N>B signature=<N>B
Field Meaning stop The response's stop_reason, verbatim wire_wait Time to first byte from the endpoint first_token Time to the first content token stream Total time spent streaming attempts Requests sent, including retries events SSE events received signature Bytes of thinking signature — measured separately because it can exceed the thinking text itself

--timing also prints --- tool calls: <name>(<id>), … when the response contained any.

Retries

A request is retried only while nothing has been emitted. Once a token has reached stdout, a transport failure is reported rather than retried, because retrying would duplicate output.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Ask one question and print only the answer:

yu exec -p "reply ok"

Measure the wire against the configured endpoint:

yu exec -p "reply ok" --timing >/dev/null

Inspect the raw blocks, which is how you see a thinking or tool_use block that the text stream would not show:

yu exec -p "what time is it in Tokyo?" --json

docs.title: yu fork
docs.text: Fork a session's record at a historical point, showing what it costs.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: yu fork --session <SESSION> --at <SEQ> --into <NEW> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning --session <SESSION> required The session whose record is branched from --at <SEQ> required The sequence number to branch at --into <NEW> required The new branch's session id --dir <DIR> .yu Where the journals live

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Creates a new session whose history is the parent's, up to and including --at. Events below the fork point are inherited by reference — they are not copied, so the new branch costs one marker line regardless of how long the parent is. The parent file is not written to.

The estimate is printed before anything is written, because two of its numbers are the decision.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
--- fork estimate
      forking delivery-1 at seq 20: 41 event(s) / 16817 bytes inherited by
      reference; the cache prefix diverges there, so a replay of this branch
      re-sends the prefix the last recorded request measured at 3324 input
      tokens; the fork itself costs 156 byte(s)
      the parent is not written to: the branch reads its history through it
Number Meaning event(s) Events the branch inherits bytes Their size, inherited by reference and not rewritten input tokens What a replay must re-send, because the prefix stops matching marker byte(s) What the fork actually writes

When no request was recorded at or before the fork point, the re-send cost is not knowable from the record and the estimate says so rather than showing a plausible number:

      … the cache prefix diverges there, so no request was recorded at or before
      the point, so the re-send cost of the prefix is not known from the record;
      the fork itself costs 156 byte(s)

After the fork:

--- forked gen2 at seq 20: 41 event(s) inherited by reference, 156 byte(s) written
--- cache prefix diverges at delivery-1:20: requests on this branch from that point onward match nothing cached
--- parent delivery-1 still holds 47 event(s), whole

A fork is not free

Everything below the fork point is shared, but from the fork point onward the cache prefix no longer matches: each request on the branch re-sends what the parent had cached. The estimate exists so that this is a decision rather than a surprise. Forking is a deliberate operation, not a debug button.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text:
Status Condition 0 The branch was created 1 --at is past the end of the parent's own events, the target name has a record already, or the parent cannot be opened

--at counts the branch's own events

On a record that is itself a fork, --at is bounded by the events in that branch's own file, not by the whole lineage.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Branch a session at sequence 20 into a new name:

yu fork --dir .yu --session delivery-1 --at 20 --into gen2

Then continue the branch:

yu decide --dir .yu --session gen2

docs.title: yu metrics
docs.text: Summarise a recorded session.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: yu metrics [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning --dir <DIR> .yu The directory holding the journals

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Reads every .jsonl file directly under --dir and prints a per-file summary to stdout. It calls no model, opens no journal through the library, and never reads the blob store — it parses each line as JSON and aggregates.

delivery-1
  events            102
  responses         12
  tool calls        31
  tool results      31  (inline 20481B, spilled 118204B)
  tokens            in=84021 out=9887 cache_read=40213
  cache hit rate    32.4%
  thinking blocks   12 (signatures kept separately: 12)
  assistant texts   12 recorded (the turn's own words, as blobs)
  reductions        {"SpillWithPointer": 4, "PassThrough": 27}
Field Meaning events Lines that parsed as events responses Model responses recorded tool calls / tool results Calls issued, and results returned inline / spilled Bytes kept inside the record, and bytes written to blobs tokens Summed over the session's responses cache hit rate cache_read / (input + cache_read). Printed only when the denominator is non-zero thinking blocks Thinking blocks, and how many carried a separately stored signature assistant texts Turns whose own words were stored as blobs reductions How many results took each reduction path. Printed only when non-empty

Files are listed in sorted order. Lines that fail to parse are skipped rather than reported, so a record with a torn final line still summarises.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status Condition 0 At least one journal was summarised 1 no journals in <dir>

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Metrics reads top-level files only

yu metrics --dir .yu reads *.jsonl directly under .yu. It does not descend into subdirectories.

This matters for yu daemon, whose sessions live one directory deeper, at .yu/<session>/<session>.jsonl. Those sessions are not summarised by this command. See Record format.

Blobs are counted, not read

spilled totals come from the bytes field recorded on each tool result. The blobs themselves are not opened, so a missing blob does not affect the summary.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
yu metrics --dir .yu

# After a daemon has been serving sessions.
yu metrics --dir .yu/s1-1759000000000-1

docs.title: yu probe
docs.text: Measure what the endpoint actually supports.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: yu probe [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning --json off Emit the report as JSON instead of a table

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Sends a series of requests to the configured endpoint and records which fields it honours, which it accepts and ignores, and which it rejects. Writes nothing to disk and opens no session.

This matters because an endpoint that accepts a field and ignores it is indistinguishable, from the client's side, from one that implements it. Without a probe, yu would believe it has a feature the endpoint does not have.

Run it against any endpoint that is not Anthropic's before trusting anything else in this manual.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A table on stdout. Each row is one capability:

================================================================================================
  CAPABILITIES  https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic  model=deepseek-flash[1m]
================================================================================================
  <support>  <feature>                                      <status>  <detail>

Followed by a section naming the design assumptions the endpoint does not support. The accepts: line under a rejected feature enumerates the variants the endpoint does model — the cheapest possible capability probe, since the endpoint reports its own vocabulary in the error.

docs.title: Saving the result
docs.text:
The JSON report is the input to the quirks profile. Save it and point yu at it so that every later run is constrained by what was measured rather than by a guess:

yu probe --json > caps.json
export YU_QUIRKS_JSON=$PWD/caps.json

See Endpoint profile.

The table and the JSON are the same report

--json changes the encoding, not the measurement. Both cost the same requests.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status Condition 0 The probe completed 1 No credential, unreachable endpoint, or a transport error

docs.title: yu run
docs.text: Run one task through the execution loop: journal, tools, reduction, shape metrics.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: yu run --task <TASK> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning -t, --task <TASK> required The task --dir <DIR> .yu Where the journal and blobs live --cwd <CWD> process working directory The directory the tools operate in -m, --model <MODEL> $ANTHROPIC_MODEL, else claude-opus-5 Model string --max-steps <N> 12 Step ceiling for the run --tools <SET> read-only read-only or full --session <SESSION> run-<UTC timestamp> The session this run belongs to --policy <PATH> none Policy TOML supplying [[reduction]] rows

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Stands up a session, offers the model a tool surface, executes what it asks for, applies the reduction rules to each tool result, and writes every step to the journal. Prints the model's final text to stdout.

The run ends when the model stops asking for tools, or when --max-steps is spent. A run that spends its step ceiling is not an error; the outcome is reported and the exit status is 0.

--tools full removes the guard rails

With full, the model can call exec, which runs sh -c with no sandbox, no timeout, and no path restriction, inheriting the environment of the process. It can do anything the process can. There is no confirmation step.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
--session names the run. Reopening a name that already has a record continues it rather than starting a new one:

--- resuming session delivery-1: 14 event(s) already recorded, continuing at seq 14

This is what a run after a crash is. Effects that the record marks as completed are read back from the record rather than performed again, so a resumed run does not repeat a write that already happened.

If the record says an effect was started but never completed, the run says so before it continues:

--- unresolved effect: write_file:notes.md@call_00_… (write 42 bytes to `notes.md`) recorded at seq 9 — the record does not say whether it happened

See Record format.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
--policy supplies a TOML file whose [[reduction]] rows replace the built-in reduction choices. Rows are evaluated in declaration order and the first match wins.

yu run --task "summarise the logs" --policy policy.toml

A row that names an axis or a path this build does not understand is not a load error. It is reported on stderr and the row is dead — it cannot match anything:

--- policy policy.toml: [[reduction]] row(s) name axis/axes this build does not understand: shape — such a row cannot match anything, so it is dead rather than merely unsatisfied

A malformed file, or an unknown top-level key, does fail the run with exit 1. See Policy file.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text:
stdout carries the model's final reply and nothing else. Everything below goes to stderr.

Line Meaning session <id> — journal in <dir> The session's address --- tool surface: <names> The tools this run was offered --- N step(s), N tool call(s), N reduction(s) in Ns Run totals --- tokens in=… out=… cache_read=… \| harness=…ms/step model_time=…ms Token accounting and overhead --- spans: <kind>=<ms> … Per-span timings --- reductions: <names> Which reduction paths fired --- shape: <signal> Shape signals, one line each --- executor context: raw material N% of M chars (…) Context composition

harness=…ms/step is the harness's own cost with model time removed: the sum of every span that is not waiting on the model, divided by the number of steps. It is NaN when the run took zero steps. This is the number that separates the cost of the harness from the cost of the model.

If no span was recorded at all, the line reads:

--- spans: NONE RECORDED (observation is not wired up)

--- shape: <signal> lines report deterministic signals — repeated identical calls, files touched outside the expected set, tokens growing without a diff. They are reported, not judged; deciding what they mean is the decision layer's job. See yu decide.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
One task with no side effects:

yu run --task "count the Rust source files under crates/" --cwd .

A named session, so a crash is recoverable:

yu run --session migrate-1 --task "rename the config key" --tools full --cwd .

Read the record back afterwards:

yu metrics --dir .yu

docs.title: Embedding the crates
docs.text: The workspace is nine crates. This page covers what each one exposes, which direction dependencies run, and where the extension points are.

docs.title: Crate graph
docs.text:
yu-cli  ──►  yu-workflow  ──►  yu-core  ──►  yu-wire
                                  │           yu-journal
                                  │           yu-tools
                                  │           yu-observe
yu-server ──►  yu-core
yu-policy ──►  injects into yu-core's traits
Crate Responsibility yu-wire Messages API: types, SSE, retries, error classification, quirks, token counting yu-journal The record: typed events, index, addressable reads, effects, replay, fork yu-core Loop, agent lifecycle, rendering, topology, scheduling, cancellation, the parallel gate yu-tools Native tools, result typing, reduction yu-policy Declarative policy resources and the script host yu-observe Spans, metrics, allocation attribution, shape signals yu-server Daemon and embedded dual mode yu-workflow Generation change, handover, human interaction yu-cli Front end and short-path bypass

Dependency direction is one-way and enforced by review, not by the compiler. yu-observe is a leaf so the wire layer can time itself without a cycle. yu-core defines traits; yu-policy injects implementations; yu-core does not depend on yu-policy.

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: Two traits are the intended seams.

docs.title: yu_core::traits::PolicySource
docs.text:
pub trait PolicySource {
    fn prompt(&self, name: &str) -> Option<String>;
    fn budget(&self, name: &str) -> Option<u64>;
    fn rule(&self, name: &str) -> Option<serde_json::Value>;
}

Implemented by yu_policy::resource::Policy. Implement it yourself to supply policy from somewhere other than a TOML file.

docs.title: yu_tools::reduce::ReductionTable
docs.text: Implemented by Policy for [[reduction]] rows. Implement it to choose reduction paths in code.

docs.title: yu_tools::Tool
docs.text:
pub trait Tool: Send + Sync {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn definition(&self) -> ToolDefinition;
    fn execute(&self, input: &Value, ctx: &ToolContext) -> ToolResult;
    fn effect(&self, _input: &Value) -> Option<EffectIntent> { None }
    fn effect_in_place(&self, _input: &Value, _ctx: &ToolContext) -> EffectVerdict {
        EffectVerdict::Unknown
    }
}

Register with ToolRegistry::register. Declaring an effect is what puts the tool under the record's intent/completion discipline; a tool that declares none is not replay-protected.

docs.title: yu-wire
docs.text:
let client = WireClient::from_env()?;                  // env-driven
let client = WireClient::builder()
    .base_url("https://api.anthropic.com")
    .auth(Auth::ApiKey(key))
    .quirks(Quirks::anthropic())
    .build()?;

let outcome = client.stream(&request, &mut sink).await?;
let response = client.send(&request).await?;
let tokens = client.count_tokens(&count_request).await?;

stream forces stream: true and retries only while nothing has been emitted. The sink is StreamSink, whose methods all have defaults. Capabilities::probe backs yu probe.

docs.title: yu-journal
docs.text:
let journal = Journal::open(dir, SessionId::new("delivery-1")).await?;
let event = journal.append(agent_id, EventBody::Note { text })?;

journal.read_from(10)?;        // seq >= 10, to the end
journal.read_range(10, 20)?;   // [10, 20)

journal.replay_seed()?;        // committed effects
journal.unresolved_effects()?; // intended, never completed
journal.estimate_fork(20)?;
Journal::open_fork(dir, session, Arc::new(parent), 20).await?;

open rebuilds the index, repairs a torn tail, and re-attaches a parent when the first event is forked.

docs.title: yu-core
docs.text:
let mut layer = DecisionLayer::new(client, journal, tools, timeline, config, charter, cwd);
let outcome = layer.run().await?;

let resumed = Resumed::read(&journal, &agent_id)?;
let mut layer = DecisionLayer::resume(resumed);

DecisionConfig::new(model) defaults to max_tokens: 8192, effort: Xhigh, max_rounds: 8, and one delegation per round. The CLI overrides the round count.

DecisionOutcome carries rounds, delegations, final_text, usage, composition, contexts, ledger, stopped_early, and outcomes, with helpers raw_material_ratio(), tool_machinery_ratio(), landing_distribution(), and landing_problems().

The execution-layer loop is yu_core::agent::{Agent, AgentConfig}; it is not re-exported at the crate root.

docs.title: yu-policy
docs.text:
let policy = Policy::from_path(Path::new("policy.toml"))?;
policy.unknown_reduction_axes();   // dead rows
policy.unknown_reduction_paths();

The tier-2 scripting surface is ScriptHost, with RhaiHost implemented. WasmtimeHost is declared and returns an unsupported error.

docs.title: yu-observe
docs.text:
let timeline = Timeline::new();
let timer = timeline.start(SpanKind::ToolExec);
// …
timer.finish();

let mut metrics = Metrics::default();
metrics.observe_spans(&timeline.spans());
metrics.harness_time_per_step_ms();

Allocator is the global allocator type; the CLI installs it.

docs.title: yu-server
docs.text:
pub enum Host {
    Embedded,
    LocalDaemon { socket: PathBuf },
    Remote { endpoint: String },
}

pub struct ServerConfig { pub host: Host, pub state_dir: PathBuf }

serve(listener, &host, config).await?;

Embedded and Remote are configuration values, not transports

The crate implements SessionHost for two types: Daemon, which owns journals, and DirectoryHost, which is metadata only. Nothing implements an in-process transport for Host::Embedded, and nothing implements Host::Remote.

To embed, drive Daemon directly in-process and skip the socket, or implement SessionHost yourself and call serve. Setting Host::Embedded in a config does not by itself avoid the socket.

docs.title: The daemon as a library
docs.text:
let daemon = Daemon::open(root)?;
let live = daemon.start("charter text")?;
live.record("human words")?;      // appends a user_message
live.unresolved()?;
live.history()?;

Live::record returns the sequence number it wrote. It does not run a turn.

For a client of the socket protocol, use yu_server::session::{Request, Response, encode_line, decode_line} over a tokio::net::UnixStream. The protocol is documented in yu daemon.

docs.title: Generation change
docs.text: yu_workflow::handover holds the handover machinery: Handover::assemble, Handover::check, Verifier::find_gaps, Trigger::should_fire, the ReaderModel trait, and NewSession::{new_session, resume_into}. WireReader is the ReaderModel implementation backed by a WireClient.

docs.title: Stability
docs.text: The workspace version is 0.0.1. Nothing here is published to crates.io, and no API is frozen. The dependency direction and the two trait seams are the parts that are treated as load-bearing.

docs.title: Endpoint compatibility
docs.text:
The Messages API is a specification. Against any endpoint but Anthropic's it is a hypothesis, and a server that accepts a field and ignores it will let a client believe it has a feature it does not have.

Everything on this page was measured, not assumed. Re-measure against your own endpoint before relying on any of it:

yu probe

Reference measurement

Endpoint https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic, model deepseek-flash[1m], measured 2026-10-10. Treat the values below as one endpoint's answers, not as properties of the API.

docs.title: Capability matrix
docs.text: Feature Status POST /v1/messages works SSE streaming works — Anthropic event names verbatim, including ping thinking always emitted, even for "reply ok" at max_tokens: 16 thinking: {type:"adaptive"} accepted thinking: {type:"adaptive", display:"summarized"} accepted thinking: {type:"enabled", budget_tokens:N} accepted — Anthropic rejects this thinking.display effect unverified — thinking text came back non-empty either way output_config.effort accepted, effect unverified output_config.format accepted, effect unverified cache_control breakpoints inert — caching is automatic Mid-conversation {"role":"system"} accepted stop_sequences accepted POST /v1/messages/count_tokens works Custom tools with input_schema works strict: true on a tool accepted tool_choice: {type:"any"} accepted — Anthropic rejects this on current models Parallel tool_use (2 in one turn) works tool_result.is_error works web_search_20260209 (server tool) works — cost 67 372 input tokens in one call web_search_20250305 accepted bash_20250124 rejected, 422 unknown variant text_editor_20250728 rejected, 422 unknown variant tool_search_tool_* + defer_loading rejected, 422 mcp_servers / mcp_toolset rejected, 422 GET /v1/models 404 context_management.edits accepted, assumed inert task_budget accepted, assumed inert fallbacks accepted, assumed inert anthropic-beta header ignored — accepted fields are accepted with or without it Authentication enforced. x-api-key works; a bad key returns 401

docs.title: What this costs
docs.text:
• Schema-less server tools are unavailable. bash_20250124 and text_editor_20250728 are both rejected, so every tool must declare an input_schema.
  • tool_search and defer_loading are unavailable, so the startup cost of a large tool surface cannot be reduced this way.
  • Server-side compaction is accepted and does nothing. Treat context_management, server compaction, and task_budget as inert. Anything that manages context has to be done client-side.
  • web_search_20260209 is the one working server tool, and it produces exactly the unbounded result shape the reduction table exists to handle.

docs.title: Quirks
docs.text: Behavioural divergences from Anthropic. Each one is something a client must special-case.

docs.title: Quirk 1 — thinking blocks must be replayed
docs.text:
Reconstructing an assistant turn without its thinking block fails:

400 invalid_request_error
The `content[].thinking` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.

The message does not name the offending message. The precise rule, established over 16 probe cases:

Case Result Fabricated tool_use id, no thinking 400 — for every id format tried Fabricated id, any thinking block 200 — the signature is not validated An id the endpoint itself issued, no thinking 200

The endpoint keeps its issued tool calls server-side and only demands the thinking block when it cannot recognise the id.

Consequences.

  1. Replay thinking blocks byte-exact. It is free, it satisfies the strict case, and it is what Anthropic's preserved thinking requires anyway. yu-wire enforces this when assembling history rather than letting a doomed request go out and fail with a confusing error.
  2. Fork and replay are feasible. Because signature is unvalidated, a forked branch may carry synthesised thinking blocks. Rewriting history does not fail the way Anthropic's preserved-thinking check would.

docs.title: Quirk 2 — identifier shapes differ
docs.text:
Anthropic This endpoint Message id msg_01… UUID, e.g. 4aeac4b3-5f44-4b94-bef3-cb721ea7bef0 tool_use id toolu_01… call_00_<base62>, e.g. call_00_4Ykgo3t3AxTqrrfx12mk4590

Nothing may parse, validate, or synthesise an id. Ids are opaque bytes and are replayed verbatim. They are also the key the endpoint indexes its issued-call record by — see Quirk 1 — so rewriting one silently changes behaviour.

docs.title: Quirk 3 — prefix caching is automatic, cache_control is inert
docs.text:
cache_creation_input_tokens is always 0. Only cache_read_input_tokens is populated. Two identical requests with the same long system prefix: the first reports cache_read=0, the second cache_read=2299. Adding an explicit cache_control breakpoint changes nothing.

Consequence: byte-stability of the rendered prefix is the entire caching mechanism. There is no breakpoint to place and no way to steer the cache. cache_control is still emitted — it is correct for Anthropic and costs nothing here — but no strategy may depend on it.

docs.title: Quirk 4 — input_tokens excludes thinking blocks
docs.text: An assistant turn carrying 86 characters of thinking and the same turn with the thinking stripped both reported input_tokens: 256. Token accounting cannot be used to detect whether thinking survived into a request.

docs.title: Quirk 5 — 422 and 400 are different failure classes
docs.text:
A malformed schema returns 422, and the message enumerates the valid variants:

422 Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type:
    tools[0]: unknown variant `bash_20250124`,
    expected `web_search_20250305` or `web_search_20260209` at line 1 column 94

This is not retryable and not a normal invalid_request_error — it means the client sent a field the endpoint does not model. yu-wire classifies it separately so it is never retried and never mistaken for a prompt bug.

It is also the cheapest possible capability probe: send a deliberately unknown variant and read the expected list back.

docs.title: Quirk 6 — 401 leaks the last 4 characters of the key
docs.text:
401 authentication_error: Authentication Fails, Your api key: ****0000 is invalid

Error bodies must be handled carefully; this one embeds key material. See Credentials.

docs.title: Streaming notes
docs.text:
• ping events are emitted between blocks and must be tolerated and skipped.
  • signature arrives as a signature_delta delta type, carried inside an ordinary content_block_delta event — it is not an event name of its own. It arrives after the thinking_deltas and before content_block_stop.
  • content_block_start for a thinking block carries "signature": "", so an accumulator must treat empty-signature-then-delta as the normal path rather than as a malformed block.
  • web_search results interleave: thinking → text → server_tool_use → web_search_tool_result → thinking → … Many blocks per turn. This is the unbounded shape the reduction table handles.

docs.title: stop_reason
docs.text: Observed: end_turn, tool_use, max_tokens. refusal and pause_turn never appeared across roughly 40 requests, and are still handled — an unhandled variant must not be silently treated as success.

docs.title: Running against Anthropic
docs.text:
Set the profile explicitly if you do not probe:

export YU_QUIRKS=anthropic

On Anthropic's endpoint the schema-less server tools are available, tool_search and defer_loading work, and cache_control breakpoints are honoured rather than inert. The probe is still the authority — measure rather than assume.

docs.title: Policy file
docs.text:
A policy is a TOML file that changes behaviour without a rebuild. It is passed with --policy on yu run and yu decide.

yu run --task "…" --policy policy.toml
yu decide --charter "…" --policy policy.toml

There is no default path and no environment variable. Without --policy, the built-in rules apply and no prediction sets are declared.

The TOML document is the policy. There is no [policy] wrapper table, and an unknown top-level key is rejected.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
All keys are optional.

Key Type Meaning prompts table, name → text Named prompt texts tool_descriptions table, tool name → text Override a tool's description roles table of tables Declarative roles topology table of tables Declarative topologies reduction array of tables Reduction rules, in priority order hooks array of tables Event → script bindings outcome_sets array of tables Prediction sets for delegations scripts table, name → source Inline script source budgets table Run ceilings

Only two of these are consumed today

[[reduction]] and [[outcome_sets]] are wired into the loop. The other seven parse, load, and are reachable through the library's accessors, but nothing in the run loop reads them yet. Writing them changes nothing.

They are documented here so the format is not a surprise when they are wired, not because they currently do anything. A file that sets [budgets] and expects the run to be bounded will not be bounded.

docs.title: [budgets]
docs.text:
Key Type max_steps integer max_input_tokens integer max_output_tokens integer max_tool_calls integer

Absent means no ceiling configured, never zero. Unknown keys here are rejected — a typo like max_input_token is a parse error, not a silently ignored line.

docs.title: [roles.<name>]
docs.text: Key Type Meaning prompt string The name of an entry in [prompts], not the text model string Model string for this role effort string low, medium, high, xhigh, or max

docs.title: [topology.<name>]
docs.text:
Key Type Meaning kind string One of the topology kinds child_role string The role children run as params table, string → string Kind-specific parameters

Topology kinds: single, chain, fan_out (alias fanout), tree, reflection, peer, verification_partition.

params values must be quoted strings — width = "4", not width = 4. Only width, consumed by fan_out, is read today. Its default is 3.

--topology does not look these up

A policy entry named [topology.review_loop] is not reachable by --topology review_loop. That flag parses a topology kind. See yu decide.

docs.title: [[reduction]]
docs.text:
Each row states a path and the axes it constrains. Rows are evaluated in declaration order and the first match wins.

[[reduction]]
path = "drop_with_manifest"
[reduction.when]
size = "large"
reproducible = "true"
Key Type path string when table, axis → value

Paths: pass_through, drop_with_manifest, spill_with_pointer, dispatch_reader (alias delegate_reader), sandbox_reduce.

Axes: kind, size, reproducible, addressable, pressure, already_on_disk, tool.

Axis Accepted values kind file, search, log, diff, structured size small, large reproducible true / yes, false / no addressable true / yes, false / no already_on_disk true / yes, false / no pressure low, high tool a tool name, e.g. exec, read_file

Axes within a row are conjunctive: every named axis must match.

An unknown axis makes a row dead, not fatal

A row naming an axis or path this build does not recognise loads without error and can never match. The CLI reports it:

--- policy policy.toml: [[reduction]] row(s) name axis/axes this build does not understand: shape — such a row cannot match anything, so it is dead rather than merely unsatisfied

Check this line. A dead row is otherwise indistinguishable from a row whose condition never came up.

docs.title: [[outcome_sets]]
docs.text:
A prediction set is the finite list of things a delegation can come back with. It is declared when the delegation is made, and the executor classifies its actual result into one of the slots. The report shrinks from prose to a choice.

[[outcome_sets]]
id = "build_result"
description = "What a build-and-test delegation can come back with."

[[outcome_sets.slots]]
name = "pass"
expects = "succeeded"

[[outcome_sets.slots]]
name = "compile_error"
expects = "failed"

[[outcome_sets.slots]]
name = "test_failure"
expects = "failed"

[[outcome_sets.slots]]
name = "no_changes_needed"
expects = "nothing_run"
Set key Type Required id string yes description string no slots array of tables yes Slot key Type Required name string yes expects string yes

docs.title: expects
docs.text:
Each slot states a claim, and the claim is checked against the record. Only claims the harness can compute are allowed.

Value Claim succeeded The run completed and every command it ran exited zero failed At least one command reported a non-zero exit status nothing_run The run completed without running a command stopped_early The run was stopped before it reported completion unchecked No claim. Not cross-checked

unchecked is how a slot opts out of the check. The others are computed, and a landing that contradicts its slot's claim is reported as a contradiction:

!! the executor landed on `delivered_and_verified`, but a command ran and failed: `echo …` exited 1

The check is bidirectional

A landing that matches its claim produces no output. A check that fired on correct runs would be worth nothing.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
The loader enforces five rules and names the set and slot it is complaining about.

  1. Set ids are unique.
  2. No slot may be named other. The name is reserved — other is always available, appended when the set is rendered, and never declared in a file.
  3. A set with no slots is an error. With nothing to land in, every result lands in other and the set is decoration.
  4. Slot names are unique within a set.
  5. A missing or malformed field names the set and the slot it is in.

Declaring no outcome_sets key is fine, and so is outcome_sets = []. Only a declared set is held to these rules.

other is where the interesting results go

A result nobody predicted is the most informative one, so the escape hatch is always present. Landing in other also widens the report budget, because that is the moment detail is worth having.

Watch the distribution. A slot that is never chosen means the set is decoration; other being common means the set is wrong.

docs.title: [[hooks]] and [scripts]
docs.text:
[[hooks]]
on = "on_handover"
script = "handover_is_worth_it"

[scripts]
handover_is_worth_it = "ctx.loose_ends > 0 || ctx.steps_since_compaction > ctx.threshold"
Hook key Type Meaning on string The event name script string The name of an entry in [scripts]

[scripts] values are inline source text, not file paths. The semantics are Rhai. A path given as a value would be evaluated as a broken Rhai expression.

Naming a script that does not exist is an error. Omitting script records the intent without arming it.

Neither is consumed today. See the warning at the top of this page.

docs.title: Load errors
docs.text: Condition Behaviour File missing Exit 1: could not read policy file `<path>`: … Malformed TOML Exit 1: policy TOML is malformed: … Unknown top-level key Exit 1, same as malformed Unknown key in [budgets] Exit 1 Outcome-set rule violation Exit 1, naming the set and slot Unknown reduction axis or path Loads. Warning on stderr, row is dead Unknown key elsewhere Ignored

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
[prompts]
decision_charter = """
You are the decision layer. You do not read code and you do not call tools.
You own completion criteria, architecture, and anything irreversible.
"""

[roles.decision]
prompt = "decision_charter"
effort = "xhigh"

[topology.review]
kind = "reflection"
child_role = "worker"

[[reduction]]
path = "drop_with_manifest"
[reduction.when]
size = "large"
reproducible = "true"

[[reduction]]
path = "spill_with_pointer"
[reduction.when]
size = "large"
reproducible = "false"
addressable = "true"

[[outcome_sets]]
id = "delivery"
description = "What a deliverable-producing delegation can come back with."

[[outcome_sets.slots]]
name = "delivered_and_verified"
expects = "succeeded"

[[outcome_sets.slots]]
name = "delivered_unverified"
expects = "nothing_run"

[[outcome_sets.slots]]
name = "blocked"
expects = "failed"

docs.title: Record format
docs.text: A session's record is an append-only JSONL file: one event per line, typed, indexed by sequence number, and addressable. It is the basis for replay as well as the memory of the run — one mechanism, two uses.

docs.title: Two layouts
docs.text:
yu daemon and the other commands write different layouts under the same --dir.

CLI. One journal per session, one shared blob store.

.yu/
  delivery-1.jsonl
  gen2.jsonl
  blobs/
    3f/
      2b9c…        (62 more hex characters)

Daemon. Each session gets its own directory.

.yu/
  daemon.sock
  s1759000000000-1/
    info.json
    s1759000000000-1.jsonl
    blobs/
      3f/
        2b9c…

The consequence to remember: yu metrics reads only top-level *.jsonl files, so daemon-owned sessions are not summarised by it.

docs.title: File naming
docs.text:
A session id becomes a file name by this rule:

  • ASCII letters, digits, -, _, and . are kept. Every other character becomes _.
  • If the result is non-empty, unchanged, and is not exactly . or .., the file is <name>.jsonl.
  • Otherwise the file is <stem>-<12 hex chars>.jsonl, where the stem is the sanitised name or the literal session when sanitisation produced nothing, and the 12 characters are the head of the SHA-256 of the original name.

So delivery-1 becomes delivery-1.jsonl, while a/b becomes a_b-<12 hex>.jsonl — which cannot collide with a session genuinely named a_b. A name like ../../etc/passwd stays a single path component.

docs.title: Blobs
docs.text:
Large payloads are stored once, outside the journal, and referenced by digest.

Property Value Digest SHA-256, lowercase hex, 64 characters Path blobs/<first 2 hex>/<remaining 62 hex> Write Temp file, then rename. A crash never leaves a half-written blob Idempotent Writing the same bytes twice stores one file

The fan-out directory is what keeps any one directory from holding every blob in a long run.

docs.title: Event envelope
docs.text:
One event per line. Field names are literal.

{
  "seq": 12,
  "ts_ms": 1759000001234,
  "session": "delivery-1",
  "agent": "executor#1",
  "body": { "event": "note", "text": "…" }
}
Field Type Meaning seq integer Position in this branch. Starts at 0 and is contiguous ts_ms integer Wall-clock milliseconds since the epoch session string The session id agent string Which agent produced the event body object Tagged by an event key

ts_ms is wall-clock rather than monotonic, because records outlive processes and must stay comparable across restarts.

docs.title: Event bodies
docs.text:
event Fields session_started charter, model, quirks user_message text model_request model, messages, digest, est_input_tokens model_response id, stop_reason, usage, blocks, thinking, text_blob tool_call tool_use_id, name, input tool_result tool_use_id, name, kind, bytes, reproducible, addressable, inline, blob, reduction injected label, blob note text effect key, description, state, tool_use_id, idempotent forked parent, parent_at_seq delegated child, depth, task session_seeded blob round_started round, ceiling

Four engineering rules are enforced by this shape:

  1. A result is not stored twice. A tool_result with both inline and blob is rejected at append time. It has one home or the other.
  2. The envelope is not repeated per content block. One event is one line; blocks are references inside it.
  3. Re-sent material is deduplicated by reference. Anything injected repeatedly — a task reminder, a charter — is stored once as a blob and referenced by digest. See injected, session_seeded.
  4. signature is stored separately from thinking text. On some endpoints a signature is longer than the text it signs, so there is no field in which the two could be joined. See thinking[].text_blob and thinking[].signature_blob.

Optional fields are omitted from the line when absent rather than written as null: model_request.est_input_tokens, model_response.text_blob, effect.tool_use_id, and the result_seq inside a completed effect.

docs.title: Effect discipline
docs.text:
A side effect is recorded before it is performed, so a crash between the two is detectable rather than silent.

{"seq":9,"body":{"event":"effect","key":"write_file:notes.md@call_00_…","description":"write 42 bytes to `notes.md`","state":"intended","idempotent":true}}

state is one of:

Value Meaning "intended" Recorded, not yet performed {"done":{"result_seq":31}} Performed; result_seq points at the tool result {"done":{}} Performed, with no result event recorded "abandoned" Recorded, deliberately not performed

On resume, only done counts as committed. An effect whose last state is intended is unresolved: the record does not say whether it happened.

--- unresolved effect: write_file:notes.md@call_00_… (write 42 bytes to `notes.md`) recorded at seq 9 — the record does not say whether it happened

A resumed run reads committed effects back from the record instead of repeating them. An unresolved effect is reported and not silently retried, because the key cannot certify that the work was not already done.

docs.title: Addresses
docs.text:
An address names one thing in the record. spot_check takes one, and a handover index is built from them.

Address Refers to blob:<digest> A blob, by its SHA-256 journal:seq=<n> The event at sequence n journal:seq=<n> (dropped by reduction) An event whose payload was dropped. Resolves to the statement that it was dropped — not an error, and not a success

An address that cannot be resolved is an error naming the address. A dropped payload is not a dangling reference; the record says what happened to it.

docs.title: Reading a record
docs.text:
# Summaries.
yu metrics --dir .yu

# One line, pretty-printed.
sed -n '13p' .yu/delivery-1.jsonl | python3 -m json.tool

# Every effect and its outcome.
grep '"event":"effect"' .yu/delivery-1.jsonl

yu fork branches a record at a sequence number; see yu fork.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Two different tool surfaces exist. An executor is offered file and shell tools; the decision layer is offered delegation and ledger tools. They do not overlap.

docs.title: Executor tools
docs.text:
Enabled by --tools. The set is fixed; there is no per-tool switch.

Tool set Tools read-only read_file, list_dir full read_file, write_file, list_dir, exec

The surface is printed at the start of a run:

--- tool surface: list_dir, read_file

docs.title: read_file
docs.text:
Read a file as UTF-8 text, relative to the working directory.

Parameter Type Required path string yes

Resolves absolute paths as given and relative paths against the working directory. Rejects non-UTF-8 content rather than lossily converting it. The result is marked reproducible and addressable: the same call returns the same bytes, and the bytes can be spilled and addressed.

docs.title: write_file
docs.text:
Write UTF-8 text to a file, creating parent directories as needed.

Parameter Type Required path string yes content string yes

Truncating overwrite. There is no append mode and no read-modify-write. Declares a non-reproducible effect: a write is a side effect and is not replayed.

docs.title: list_dir
docs.text:
List one directory's entries, sorted, directories suffixed with /.

Parameter Type Required path string no — defaults to .

Non-recursive. One level only.

docs.title: exec
docs.text:
Run a shell command with sh -c in the working directory; stdout, stderr and the exit code are captured.

Parameter Type Required command string yes

The result is rendered as:

$ <command>
exit: <code>
stdout (<n> bytes):
<stdout>
stderr (<n> bytes):
<stderr>

When the process was killed by a signal, the marker line is exit: terminated by signal — no exit code is invented.

exec is unsandboxed

No chroot, no path jail, no allow-list, no timeout. .. is not blocked and absolute paths are honoured. The command inherits the environment of the yu process and runs with its privileges. stdin is /dev/null.

Output is captured in full and bounded only afterwards, by the reduction layer. See Reduction.

docs.title: Conditional executor tools
docs.text:
Tool Offered when delegate The run is permitted to derive agents — see Delegation depth land The delegation was launched with a prediction set

An executor's delegate takes task (required) and items (optional, the places to cover).

land classifies the run's own outcome: slot (the name of the slot it landed in, or other) and why (the reason, in the executor's words). Both required.

docs.title: Decision layer tools
docs.text:
Fixed set, in fixed order. The order is part of the cache prefix, so it does not vary between runs.

Tool Purpose delegate Hand a self-contained task to a fresh executor decide Record a decision or a rejection into the ledger retire Remove an entry from the ledger, with a reason spot_check Pull one thing out of the record, by address

ask_human is specified and not built. It has no schema and no dispatch; calling it returns an error naming the four tools that exist.

docs.title: delegate
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required task string yes question string no items array of string no expected_files array of string no outcomes string, one of the policy's set ids yes, iff the policy declares at least one set

When the policy declares no outcome sets, outcomes is removed from the schema entirely and only task is required. When it declares sets, outcomes is required and its value is constrained to the declared ids — the layer chooses from a list, it cannot invent a set.

A delegation that names no set, or an unknown one, is refused with an error result rather than run.

The delegation returns a report: the executor's final text, its evidence (commands and exit codes), shape signals, an omitted-item manifest, step and token counts, its landing, and any contradiction the harness found.

docs.title: decide
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required what string yes why string yes verdict accepted or rejected yes

Writes to the ledger (L1). accepted records a decision; rejected records a ruled-out proposal, which is what stops the layer re-proposing something it already dismissed.

what is the entry's identity: retire later matches it exactly. A repeat of the same what is reported and not recorded twice. Reversing a verdict is recorded as a reversal, with both reasons.

docs.title: retire
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required item string yes reason string yes

Removes an entry, matched by its exact text — a decision's or rejection's what, an open question, or a roster entry. This is the only mechanism that shrinks the ledger.

docs.title: spot_check
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required address string yes

Resolves one address and loads it into the decision layer's own context. This is the only channel by which raw material reaches that layer, and its cost is charged there — it is a scarce action, not a reading habit.

Address forms are in Record format.

docs.title: Delegation depth
docs.text:
An executor may derive further executors. The ceiling is 3 levels below the decision layer:

decision
  └ executor#1
      └ executor#2
          └ executor#3      ← at the ceiling

An executor at the ceiling is not offered delegate at all. If the model calls the name anyway, it is answered without an error:

there is no `delegate` here: derivation stops at 3 levels, and this run is at the last one. Do the work here, or report what you could not do and why.

docs.title: Reduction
docs.text:
A tool result is not a string. It carries a kind, a size, whether it can be reproduced, whether it can be addressed, and which tool produced it. The path taken is chosen from those axes plus the current context pressure.

Axis Values kind file, search, log, diff, structured size small (≤ 8192 bytes), large reproducible true / false addressable true / false pressure low (fill < 0.75), high already_on_disk true / false tool the producing tool's name, e.g. exec Path What happens pass_through The result goes through unchanged drop_with_manifest Dropped, with a manifest saying how much was dropped and the command to re-run spill_with_pointer Written to the blob store, replaced by a pointer carrying instructions dispatch_reader A shape-specialised reader agent is dispatched. Alias: delegate_reader sandbox_reduce Reduced inside a sandbox; only the reduced result returns

Built-in thresholds: inline_limit is 8192 bytes and reader_limit is 2048 bytes. A policy's [[reduction]] rows replace the built-in choice for the rows they match. See Policy file.

Every reduction is an explicit event in the record. A manifest states what was left out rather than approximating it.
